from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "All signals decompose into simple sine waves.",
            "A short pulse requires infinite frequencies.",
            "A pure sine wave lasts forever."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Intuition", lecture_lines)
        
        # Initialize objects for animations
        circle = Circle(radius=1.0, color="#FF5733")
        sine_wave = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(3 * x), x_range=[-2, 2], color="#33FF57")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF5733"))
        self.place_at_grid(circle, 'C3')
        self.play(Create(circle))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#33FF57"))
        # Visualize pulse contraction (simulated by scaling circle)
        self.play(circle.animate.scale(0.2).set_color("#33FF57"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#33FF57"))
        self.play(FadeOut(circle))
        self.place_at_grid(sine_wave, 'C3', scale_factor=1.5)
        self.play(Create(sine_wave))
        
        # Highlight peaks and troughs
        peak_dot = Dot(color=YELLOW).move_to(sine_wave.point_from_proportion(0.25))
        trough_dot = Dot(color=YELLOW).move_to(sine_wave.point_from_proportion(0.75))
        self.play(FadeIn(peak_dot), FadeIn(trough_dot))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Defining the Trade-off: Time-Frequency Reciprocity", 
                          ["We define the uncertainty principle as product inequality.", 
                           "Narrower in time spreads frequency wider.", 
                           "Wider in time concentrates frequency tighter."])
        
        # Setup signals
        time_axis = Line(self.grid['B1'], self.grid['B4'], color=GRAY)
        freq_axis = Line(self.grid['E1'], self.grid['E4'], color=GRAY)
        
        self.add(time_axis, freq_axis)
        
        # Gaussian functions
        def gaussian(x, sigma):
            return np.exp(-x**2 / (2 * sigma**2))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#33FFF5")
        time_gauss = FunctionGraph(lambda x: gaussian(x, 0.5), x_range=[-2, 2], color="#33FFF5")
        self.place_at_grid(time_gauss, 'B2', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(Create(time_gauss))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#33FFF5")
        
        # Squeezing time signal
        tight_gauss = FunctionGraph(lambda x: gaussian(x, 0.2), x_range=[-2, 2], color="#FF5733")
        wide_freq = FunctionGraph(lambda x: gaussian(x, 1.0), x_range=[-2, 2], color="#33FFF5")
        
        self.place_at_grid(tight_gauss, 'B2', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(wide_freq, 'E2', scale_factor=0.5)
        
        self.play(Transform(time_gauss, tight_gauss), FadeIn(wide_freq))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#33FFF5")
        
        wide_gauss = FunctionGraph(lambda x: gaussian(x, 1.0), x_range=[-2, 2], color="#FF5733")
        tight_freq = FunctionGraph(lambda x: gaussian(x, 0.2), x_range=[-2, 2], color="#33FFF5")
        
        self.place_at_grid(wide_gauss, 'B2', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(tight_freq, 'E2', scale_factor=0.5)
        
        self.play(Transform(time_gauss, wide_gauss), Transform(wide_freq, tight_freq))
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "The Gaussian is the optimal signal.",
            "It minimizes uncertainty in both domains.",
            "Rectangular windows create messy sidelobes.",
            "Gaussians decay smoothly without ringing.",
            "They are mathematically the most efficient."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing the Gaussian Optimal", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define mobjects
        gaussian = FunctionGraph(lambda x: np.exp(-x**2), x_range=[-3, 3], color="#F5FF33")
        rect = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 1 if -1 < x < 1 else 0, x_range=[-3, 3], color="#33FFCC")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#F5FF33"))
        self.place_in_area(gaussian, "B1", "C3", scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(Create(gaussian))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#F5FF33"))
        # Visualize narrowing/widening while preserving area
        gauss_tracker = ValueTracker(1.0)
        gaussian.add_updater(lambda m: m.become(FunctionGraph(
            lambda x: (1/gauss_tracker.get_value()) * np.exp(-(x/gauss_tracker.get_value())**2),
            x_range=[-3, 3], color="#F5FF33"
        ).move_to(self.grid["B2"]).scale(0.7)))
        self.play(gauss_tracker.animate.set_value(0.5), run_time=2)
        self.play(gauss_tracker.animate.set_value(1.5), run_time=2)
        gaussian.clear_updaters()
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#33FFCC"))
        self.place_in_area(rect, "B4", "C6", scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(Create(rect))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#F5FF33"))
        # Highlight smooth decay
        highlight = Circle(radius=0.5, color=WHITE).move_to(self.grid["B2"])
        self.play(Create(highlight))
        self.play(FadeOut(highlight))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#F5FF33"))
        # Show final optimal label
        label = Text("Optimal Bound", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(label, "D4")
        self.play(Write(label))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Application: Radar and Chirp Signals", [
            "Short pulses resolve time, not frequency.", 
            "Long signals resolve frequency, not time.", 
            "Chirps combine both for better radar."
        ])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Represent a short pulse
        pulse = VGroup(
            Line(ORIGIN, UP*1, color=BLUE),
            Line(UP*1, RIGHT*0.2+UP*1, color=BLUE),
            Line(RIGHT*0.2+UP*1, RIGHT*0.2, color=BLUE)
        )
        self.place_at_grid(pulse, "C2")
        self.play(Create(pulse))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)

        chirp = FunctionGraph(lambda x: np.sin(x**2), x_range=[0, 3], color="#FF33A8")

        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF33A8")
        self.wait(1)

        label = Text("Peak", font_size=16, color=YELLOW)

        self.place_at_grid(peak_group, "E4")

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion: The Fundamental Trade-off", ["Localization in both domains is impossible.", "This is a fundamental wave property.", "Physics trade-offs are unavoidable constraints."])
        
        # --- Visual Setup ---
        # Represent the seesaw balance of Time vs Frequency
        seesaw_base = Triangle().scale(0.5).set_fill(GREY, 1)
        seesaw_bar = Line(LEFT*2, RIGHT*2, color=WHITE)
        
        # Time Precision (left side) and Frequency Precision (right side)
        time_text = Text("Time Precision", font_size=20, color=BLUE)
        freq_text = Text("Frequency Precision", font_size=20, color=YELLOW)
        
        seesaw = VGroup(seesaw_base, seesaw_bar)
        
        self.place_at_grid(seesaw, "D3", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.place_at_grid(time_text, "C2", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(freq_text, "C5", scale_factor=0.8)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.play(Write(seesaw), Write(time_text), Write(freq_text))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        # Animate the seesaw tilting to show inverse relationship
        self.play(Rotate(seesaw_bar, angle=PI/8, about_point=seesaw_bar.get_center()),
                  time_text.animate.shift(UP*0.5),
                  freq_text.animate.shift(DOWN*0.5))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        # Stabilize
        self.play(Rotate(seesaw_bar, angle=-PI/8, about_point=seesaw_bar.get_center()),
                  time_text.animate.shift(DOWN*0.5),
                  freq_text.animate.shift(UP*0.5))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Uncertainty Principle: The Fourier Trade-off

sections.title: Prerequisite Intuition: The Pulse and the Sine Wave
sections.content: Briefly revisit the Fourier Transform foundation: Any signal can be decomposed into sine waves. Introduce the extreme ends: a single 'spike' (Dirac delta) in time requires infinite frequencies to construct, while a single perfect sine wave exists for infinite time.
sections.example: Visualizing a 'snap' (short burst of sound) versus a 'pure hum' (tuning fork tone).

sections.title: Defining the Trade-off: Time-Frequency Reciprocity
sections.content: Introduce the Uncertainty Principle in signals: $\Delta t \cdot \Delta f \geq C$. Explain that narrowing the window in the time domain necessarily widens the spread in the frequency domain. Use animation to show the 'squeezing' of a Gaussian pulse.
sections.example: Animation of a 'rubber band' pulse: compressing it horizontally in the time-axis causes it to 'pop' and expand vertically in the frequency spectrum.

sections.title: Visualizing the Gaussian Optimal
sections.content: Highlight why the Gaussian function is the 'Goldilocks' signal—it is the only function that achieves the minimum possible uncertainty bound. Show a side-by-side graphical comparison of a rectangular window vs. a Gaussian window.
sections.example: A character 'Dr. Fourier' demonstrating how the Gaussian shape minimizes 'spill-over' (sidelobes) in both time and frequency.

sections.title: Application: Radar and Chirp Signals
sections.content: Apply the principle to real-world technology. Explain the dilemma: short pulses provide high resolution for distance (time) but lose precision in identifying velocity (frequency). Introduce the 'Chirp' signal as a clever workaround.
sections.example: A bat using 'chirps': explaining how the frequency sweep allows the bat to determine both exact distance and relative speed of a moth despite the uncertainty limit.

sections.title: Conclusion and Summary
sections.content: Synthesize the core takeaway: You cannot perfectly localize a signal in both domains. This isn't a failure of our tools, but a fundamental property of wave mathematics.
sections.example: A final graphic showing a 'See-Saw' balancing act: as Time Precision goes up, Frequency Precision must go down.
